region: Romulus · Cayuga Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Goose Watch Winery sits on the western shore of Cayuga Lake near Romulus, its tasting room set in a restored century-old barn with a deck looking out over the water. It belongs to the Peterson family, who also own Swedish Hill Winery, and it has made a point of “taking the path less travelled.” Rather than lean on the region’s usual grapes, it works with less common European varieties and with grapes bred at Cornell University, alongside sparkling, fortified and ice wines.

Crimson Brut is something of a rarity in the Finger Lakes: a dry red sparkling wine. It blends Lemberger, the Central European grape known in Austria as Blaufränkisch, with Chambourcin, a French-American hybrid that ripens reliably in cool climates and brings deep color and bright acidity. The winery describes complex dark-berry aromas with hints of black pepper, a spicy note Lemberger is known for.

Red sparkling wine has deep roots elsewhere, from Lambrusco in Emilia-Romagna to sparkling Shiraz in Australia, and it is classically served lightly chilled alongside rich, savory food. Crimson Brut brings the idea to Cayuga Lake. According to the winery, it has won a silver medal at the Finger Lakes International Wine Competition and 89 points at the New York Wine Classic.
